summary: The statement and proof are mathematically valid. The Pell-grid counts, line-mass exclusion, original-law tail bound, minimum-area core containment, lattice-point area estimate, and maximum-triangle determinant bound establish the stated constants for every integer t >= 100. The inverse-matrix estimate supplies a nonzero competitor in the exact transported lattice, so its norm bounds every genuine shortest vector, including ties; the transported tilt then yields the claimed uniform vanishing score. The predecessor facts are used only to identify the core, affine-map, lattice, and score conventions, with explicit matching definitions; none of their near-stationarity conclusions is invoked.
